newsitem.title: SYRIA: Syrian paper says Israel planning more bombings.
newsitem.headline: Syrian paper says Israel planning more bombings.

text.p: An official Syrian newspaper said on Monday Israel was planning more bombings in Syria and warned Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu that the wave of terror would not exclude Israel.

"The Netanyahu government would be mistaken if it thinks that it is able to preserve its security by threatening the security and stability of others through committing massacres against innocent civilians," Mohammed Khair al-Wadi, director-general of the Tishreen daily, wrote.
Syria has accused Israel of responsibility for the bombing of a bus in central Damascus last week in which 11 people were killed and 42 injured. Israel denied the charge.
"In order to close the door on the peace process completely, the Netanyahu government resorted to ugly crimes against Syrian buses in Syria and Lebanon," Wadi said.
"It has become clear to all that Israel had committed these crimes and is planning to commit new terrorist operations...
"With this the Netanyahu government would drag the region into a new cycle of violence, terrorism, tension and the danger of war...this cycle will not exclude Israel," he said.

Last month there was a machinegun attack against a bus carrying Syrian workers in Lebanon. The Lebanese government said Israeli-linked hardline Christians were behind the attack that killed one person.
Syria has held sporadic peace talks with Israel since 1991 but no negotiations were held since Netanyahu took office in June.
Syria strongly condemned Netanyahu's refusal to swap the occupied Arab lands for peace and said it would not return to the negotiations until Netanyahu changed his policies on peace.
